summary: Reuse only the indexed object/path kernel. Store means Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/EvidenceStore.swift; Lifecycle and Retention mean the corresponding EvidenceObjectLifecycleTests.swift and EvidenceRetentionLifecycleTests.swift under Tests/DiskStewardCoreTests/EvidenceStore in the frozen snapshot.

findings.claim: Partial snapshots must publish supplied positives while missing objects remain unknown, non-actionable and tied to their prior observation. Complete recovery may then delete them. Generation failed-root cleanup would erase valid legacy positives.
findings.recommendation: Retain original rootCoverage and every supplied entry. Gate absence on complete coverage and unchanged scope. Add legacy partial replacement and mixed-root hard-link cases.

findings.claim: Tests require one physical hard-link object, stable canonical selection, non-actionability while linked, actionable single-link recovery, scopeEnter/scopeExit without deletion, and no repeated unchanged state-history rows.
findings.recommendation: Reuse immutable-prior comparison, per-binding coverage, unknown rebasing and one state insertion per changed object while preserving these identity/scope semantics.

findings.claim: The legacy replacement test requires exactly one replace event, conflicting with corrected incoming-addition plus retired-object-debit accounting. Legacy also returns complete arrays; generation results are bounded. Legacy processes observed objects by path, but multi-event ordering is not strongly pinned by tests.
findings.recommendation: Intentionally update replacement expectations to net delta and separate object traceability. Preserve deterministic ordering and complete legacy results unless explicitly changing that contract; do not silently inherit the 2048-row window.

findings.claim: The reusable boundary is after generation proof validation/deduplication and before generation finalization. Calling the full generation publisher would invent pass requirements, run filesystem validation, map partial coverage to failure and alter scan lifecycle. Legacy tests use synthetic paths without pass IDs.
findings.recommendation: Extract a transaction-local indexed object/path kernel with observation context, scope/coverage and a trusted SQL input relation. Generation supplies validated staging; legacy supplies an indexed TEMP relation without generation foreign keys or fake passes. Abstract fixed staging readers without another generation-sized copy. Keep proof checks and source cleanup in callers; do not alter an active generation for legacy input.

findings.claim: Legacy wrapper semantics include scope/duplicate-coverage rejection before writes, replay without new events, startup offline gaps and limitation-derived partial gaps. Its eventGap lifecycle and result assembly differ from generation publication.
findings.recommendation: Keep each wrapper's validation, replay, observation/snapshot/gap writes and result assembly around the shared kernel in one transaction. Test rollback, reopen replay, entry-cap recovery and active-generation coexistence; clean temporary inputs without touching durable staging.
